mapping_basis: The readiness record supplied no stanza labels and all captions are empty. Every photo was inspected full frame and compared to the canonical Sanskrit; only specific visual correspondences were mapped. The complete observation record is kept in task data under reference-mapping-v001.json.
source_photo_role: User-supplied images are read-only story/context references, never generated art, style anchors or approvals.

references.observed_reference: Diagram explicitly contrasts sattva, rajas and tamas, labelled with Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva.
references.mapping_note: Direct visual match for the qualities named in stanza 1.

references.observed_reference: Rural worker, animals and birds share repeated divine visages, an image of the Lord present among different beings.
references.mapping_note: Fits the stanza's equal-minded worship of the Lord in all beings.

references.observed_reference: A blue divine ascetic and a companion stand before a seated praying sage.
references.mapping_note: Likely Nārāyaṇa and Nara visiting Mārkaṇḍeya; the source art does not name the figures, so confidence is medium.

references.observed_reference: A blue infant on a banyan leaf floats in floodwater while a sage reaches toward him.
references.mapping_note: Specific match for the deluge and banyan-leaf infant in stanza 7.

references.observed_reference: An ascetic gestures toward a small planetary cosmology.
references.mapping_note: Symbolic match for the worlds seen inside the infant's breath in stanza 8; confidence is medium.

references.observed_reference: Shiva and Parvati appear together in a mountainous landscape.
references.mapping_note: Specific pair named in stanza 9; the source image also contains a separate devotional Shiva panel.

references.observed_reference: A diagram shows worlds above and below a central earthly mountain.
references.mapping_note: Schematic match for the hierarchy of worlds and Vaikuṇṭha beyond them; confidence is medium.

unmapped_extras.reason: Adult Viṣṇu reclining on Ananta is not a specific scene in these ten stanzas and is distinct from the infant-on-banyan-leaf vision.
A devotee worships a Śiva lingam; the image does not identify Mārkaṇḍeya or depict the meeting with Śiva and Gaurī.
The Krishna-and-gopis dance is not a grounded depiction of the apsaras' attempt to distract Mārkaṇḍeya.
